subject: english-language
source_note: Topic structure follows the AQA A-Level English Language specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: The analytical methods for unpicking how texts represent groups underpin the study of social and regional diversity
Representation in individual texts scales up to the wider public discourses about language
How an individual acquires language parallels how a whole language evolves over time
Attitudes captured in diversity study are exactly the prejudices and debates examined in language discourses
Public anxieties about 'declining' English are a recurring theme in both change and discourses
Synchronic variation across speakers and diachronic change over time are two faces of the same variability
Understanding how writers craft representation informs students' own evaluative and discursive writing
Writing skills are assessed through directed responses that intervene in language discourses
Diversity provides the theoretical frameworks students apply when designing their own investigation
Child language is a popular, well-theorised topic for the independent investigation
Both NEA tasks reward methodical analysis of data and conscious, audience-aware crafting of language
The discursive writing built in the exam units underpins the deliberate stylistic choices of original writing
Historical change offers rich corpora for a data-driven independent investigation
